newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN LOOK FOR COMPENSATION AGAINST SAMPDORIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN LOOK FOR COMPENSATION AGAINST SAMPDORIA.

text.p: Italian champions AC Milan face a difficult away game on Sunday against Sampdoria, just four days after their shock 3-2 home defeat by Portuguese side Porto in a Champions League tie.
Despite that setback, however, club owner Silvio Berlusconi rejected criticism of his side and its new coach, Uruguyan Oscar Washington Tabarez.
"I saw an excellent Milan, especially in the first half, a side capable of playing some good soccer but which then rather fell apart," Berlusconi said.
"But, I'm not worried, we're at the beginning of the season...Tabarez can work away without worrying."
Tabarez, grateful for the vote of confidence from his boss, believes Milan were guilty of concentration lapses against Porto.
"When you are playing at home and you take the lead but then concede two goals, it's a sign that your concentration is not right," he said.
Against Sampdoria, Milan will be without injured captain Franco Baresi and suspended Montenegrin schemer Dejan Savicevic but will probably field Liberian striker George Weah.

Having picked up a finger cut that required four stitches while scoring Milan's second goal against Porto, Weah had seemed an unlikely starter against Sampdoria but is now expected to recover in time.

Weah will be partnered by Marco Simone and Roberto Baggio in attack with Frenchman Marcel Desailly, Croat Zvonimir Boban and Demetrio Albertini in midfield in a line up identical to that which started against Porto.
In defence, Tabarez may be tempted to replace central defender Filippo Galli with 37-year-old Pietro Vierchowod, bought last week but yet to make his debut for Milan.

Sampdoria, beaten 1-0 by Perugia in their seasonal opener last Sunday, are without suspended Serb midfielder Sinisa Mihajlovic but could still field four foreigners -- Argentine striker Juan Veron and Frenchmen Christian Karembeu, Pierre Laigle and Oumar Dieng.
European Champions Juventus, impressive 1-0 Champions League midweek winners against England's Manchester United, are in bouyant mood for their home game against Cagliari.
Juventus coach Marcello Lippi said that not only Wednesday's goalscorer, Croat striker Alen Boksic, but also the whole team was playing well.
"The media say that it was Boksic's night. Sure, he played very well, he scored a goal, but as far as I'm concerned it was everybody's night, not just Boksic's," he said.

Against Cagliari, the Croat striker will once again be partnered by Alessandro Del Piero and Christian Vieri, while Angelo Di Livio is on standby to take over from Antonio Conte in midfield should the latter's appeal against a two-day ban fail.

Cagliari have a distinctly Uruguyan flavour about them since not only coach Gregorio Perez but also three players likely to feature against Juventus -- midfielder Fabian O'Neill and strikers Luis Romero and Dario Silva -- are Uruguyan.
Swiss internationals, goalkeeper Marco Pascolo and defender Ramon Vega, and Danish midfielder Christian Lonstrup, further add to Cagliari's cosmopolitan look.
Internazionale, midweek 3-0 UEFA Cup winners away to French side Guingamp, will also field a multinational side for their home tie with newly promoted Perugia.
Argentine Javier Zanetti, Swiss Ciriaco Sforza, Englishman Paul Ince, Chilean Ivan Zamorano and Frenchmen Joceyln Angloma and Youri Djorkaeff are all expected to start against Perugia.
The newly promoted side field their own intriguing line up, including Yugoslav goalkeeper Alexandar Kocic, Croat midfielder Milan Rapajic and Dutch midfielder Michel Kreek.
Italy's other European protagonists, Lazio, AS Roma and Parma who all won midweek UEFA Cup ties, have potentially awkward games against Udinese, Vicenza and Piacenza respectively.

Fiorentina, who drew 1-1 away to Romanian side Gloria Bistrita in a Thursday Cup Winners' Cup tie, will want to forget their opening 4-2 league defeat by Vicenza last Sunday when facing Atalanta in Bergamo.
Fiorentina will be without suspended defender Daniele Carnasciali but again rely on their impressive strike force of Argentine Gabriel Batistuta and Brazilian Oliveira.
